1

AI Graphics Fundamentals

Understand what AI-generated graphics are and how AI works

Start here. Learn the basics of AI image generation, prompts and reference images before you create anything.

What Are AI-Generated Graphics?
+

AI-generated graphics are images created or modified with artificial intelligence. Instead of manually creating everything, you give AI an idea, prompt, or reference image, and it helps produce the visual.

  • Think of AI as your creative assistant — not the designer.
Understanding AI Image Generators
+

AI image tools mainly do three things:

  • Text → Image: describe an idea and AI creates it
  • Image → Image: give AI an image and change it
  • Image + Text → Image: give AI a reference and explain what to change
How AI Understands Prompts
+

A prompt is an instruction you give AI. Instead of "A woman," give more direction.

  • “A confident woman wearing a black suit, standing in a modern office, cinematic lighting, professional atmosphere.”

The more clearly you describe the important parts, the more control you have.

Reference Images
+

Reference images help AI understand what you want — faces, characters, clothing, poses, lighting, colors, composition and style.

  • References are especially useful when you want the same character or visual style across multiple graphics.
Common AI Mistakes
+

AI can produce bad hands, extra fingers, distorted faces, broken text, poor anatomy and inconsistent characters.

  • Don’t start over. Find the problem → tell AI what to fix → regenerate or edit.

Prompting for Graphics

Direct the image like an art director, not just write prompts

Master the skills to control exactly what AI produces.

Think Like an Art Director
+

Before creating an image, ask:

  • What am I creating?
  • Who is it for?
  • What should people notice first?
  • What should it feel like?
  • What should the subject look like?

You are not just writing prompts — you are directing the image.

What to Control in a Prompt
+
  • Subject — who or what is in the image
  • Composition — where everything should be
  • Camera — close-up, wide shot, low angle
  • Lighting — soft, dramatic, cinematic, neon, studio
  • Environment — where is the scene
  • Colors — what palette to use
  • Mood — luxury, mystery, excitement, professionalism
  • Clothing & Pose — what the subject wears and does
  • Style — realistic, cinematic, 3D, illustrated
  • Aspect Ratio — 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9
  • Negative Instructions — what AI should avoid
Basic Prompt Formula
+

Subject + Environment + Composition + Lighting + Style + Mood

  • “A confident woman in a black suit, standing in a futuristic office, centered composition, cinematic lighting, premium realistic style, mysterious mood.”

Don’t make every prompt extremely long. Clear beats complicated.

AI Character Creation

Create consistent characters and turn them into campaigns

Build original characters with AI and keep them consistent across poses, outfits and projects.

Create Your Character
+

Define: face, skin tone, hair, clothing, body type, personality and distinctive features.

Keep the Character Consistent
+

Use reference images and consistent descriptions to maintain facial features, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions and overall identity.

Create Character Variations & Campaign
+

Put the same character into different poses, environments, outfits and expressions. Then turn one character into a full campaign:

  • Character → Poster → Profile Picture → Advertisement → Social Graphics
6

AI Image Editing

Edit existing images instead of starting from scratch

AI can change what needs changing while keeping what already works.

What AI Can Edit
+
  • Change clothing
  • Change backgrounds
  • Add or remove objects
  • Change poses
  • Fix hands
  • Improve faces
  • Change lighting
  • Extend images
  • Change colors
  • Upscale images

Golden rule: change what needs changing. Keep what already works.

7

Designing Like a Professional

AI creates the image. Design makes it a professional graphic

The design principles that turn a beautiful AI image into a professional graphic.

The Principles of Professional Design
+
  • Visual Hierarchy — make the most important element stand out first
  • Typography — readable fonts, proper sizing, spacing and alignment
  • Contrast — make important elements easy to see
  • Composition — balance elements, avoid clutter
  • Color — colors that work together and support the message
  • Spacing — give elements room to breathe
  • Branding — keep colors, fonts, logos and style consistent
  • Storytelling — a graphic should communicate an idea or emotion, not just look pretty

01 Professional Graphic

Copy this prompt into any AI image tool

Create a premium corporate announcement graphic for a company called NEXORA GROUP. Show a confident young Black woman with neat Fulani braids wearing a tailored black double-breasted blazer and black trousers, standing beside a desk with a laptop in a modern luxury office. Large floor-to-ceiling windows reveal a sophisticated city skyline in the background. Use warm cinematic lighting, dark charcoal and gold branding, elegant editorial composition, realistic photography, professional corporate atmosphere. Add the headline “Driven by Vision. Built for Impact.” in large elegant typography, with smaller text “Building solutions that shape the future.” Include the tagline “INNOVATE. ELEVATE. LEAD.” and subtle corporate icons at the bottom. Premium, polished, high-end business campaign aesthetic, vertical poster.

AI Ethics, Copyright & Licensing

Create responsibly — know who owns what you make

The rules, rights and responsibilities that matter when you design for yourself or for clients.

Who Owns AI-Generated Work
+
  • Ownership depends on the tool and the plan you use (free vs paid).
  • Most commercial tools give you full rights to the images you generate.
  • Always check each tool's terms before selling work made with it.
  • Keep a record of what you generated in case you need to prove it.
    • The Ethics of Using AI
    +
  • Never use a real person's likeness (face, voice, identity) without permission.
  • Avoid trademarked brands, logos and characters in work you sell.
  • Be culturally sensitive when depicting people and cultures.
  • Don't pass AI images off as human-created without disclosure.
    • Watermarks, Disclosure & Platform Rules
    +
  • Many platforms now require labelling AI-generated content.
  • Keep the original prompt and generation data as proof.
  • Follow each tool's and platform's disclosure rules.
  • When in doubt, tell your client the image is AI-generated.
    • 12

    Export, Resolution & File Formats

    Ship clean, usable files for any platform or client

    Know exactly how to save and size your designs so they look sharp everywhere.

    When to Use Each File Format
    +
  • PNG — logos, transparency and crisp graphics.
  • JPG — photos and smaller file sizes.
  • WebP — modern web use, best quality-to-size.
  • SVG — vector art that scales to any size.
  • PDF — print-ready documents and flyers.
    • Resolution & DPI: Print vs Web
    +
  • Web uses 72–96 DPI; print needs 300 DPI.
  • Upscale small AI images with an upscaler before printing.
  • Never stretch a low-resolution image — it goes blurry.
  • Design large and scale down, not the other way around.
    • Export Presets for Each Platform
    +
  • Instagram Story: 1080×1920 (9:16).
  • Instagram Post: 1080×1080 (1:1) or 1080×1350 (4:5).
  • Facebook/LinkedIn share: 1200×627.
  • YouTube thumbnail: 1280×720.
  • Print: 300 DPI at final physical size.
    • 13

    Design Workflow & Organization

    Work like a professional, not just a designer

    The habits and systems professionals use to stay consistent, organised and client-ready.

    Build a Brand Kit
    +
  • Define one color palette and stick to it.
  • Pick 1–2 fonts for headings and body.
  • Create a simple style guide of what the brand looks like.
  • Keep logos, colors and fonts consistent across everything.
    • File & Asset Management
    +
  • Name files clearly (project-purpose-version).
  • Keep original files separate from edited versions.
  • Use versioning (v1, v2, final) so nothing gets lost.
  • Organise folders by client or project.
    • Taking a Client Brief
    +
  • Capture the goal, audience and message first.
  • Ask what they like and dislike as reference.
  • Clarify deadlines, format and usage rights.
  • Deliver on time and over-communicate progress.
    • 14

    Career & Monetization

    Turn your AI design skill into real income

    The money paths most courses never teach — freelancing, products and print-on-demand.

    Freelance Foundations
    +
  • Find clients through your network, social media and referrals.
  • Scope clearly — what you will and won't deliver.
  • Price your work fairly: time + skill + value.
  • Use contracts so you and the client agree upfront.
    • Sell Designs, Presets & Prompt Packs
    +
  • Create and sell prompt packs, presets and templates.
  • Package your best work into sellable downloads.
  • List on marketplaces or your own store.
  • One product can sell again and again.
    • Print-on-Demand & Merch
    +
  • Turn your designs into T-shirts, mugs and posters.
  • Use print-on-demand platforms with no inventory.
  • Design in print-safe, high-resolution formats.
  • Test small and scale what sells.
    • Portfolio & Selling Your Services
    +
  • Showcase your best work in a clean portfolio.
  • Offer clear packages — single graphic, campaign, branding.
  • Ask satisfied clients for testimonials and referrals.
  • Keep improving and re-pricing as your skills grow.
    • 15

    AI Automation for Design

    Design at scale with automation

    Use AI tools and agents to generate briefs, prompts and design systems at scale.

    Automate Repetitive Design Tasks
    +
  • Automate batch resizing, variants and repeated edits.
  • Use presets and templates for common jobs.
  • Let AI handle the repeated steps, you focus on the creative.
    • Use Agents to Generate Briefs & Prompts at Scale
    +
  • Use AI agents (like CREAO) to generate design briefs in bulk.
  • Generate whole prompt libraries quickly from one idea.
  • Automate research, moodboards and art direction.
    • Build a Repeatable Design System
    +
  • Turn one strong design into a system.
  • Reuse layouts, palettes and templates across a client's work.
  • Automate delivery so one project becomes many.
    • AI helps you create the image. Design helps you create the graphic. Art direction helps you create something people remember.
